Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: HIPAA access controls, BAA availability and hosting options — action summary

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Summary of what we covered (short):
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II (most recent audit completed 2025). I added the audit scope to the attached BAA summary.
- BAA availability: we are able to sign a standard BAA; typical turnaround for legal review + DocuSign is ~2–4 weeks once we have PO/statement of intent.
- PHI handling boundaries: Hosted (public) API is not appropriate for PHI by default. Eligible options we discussed: Dedicated (reserved capacity) with VPC peering or private tenant, or Redwood Private (VPC-controlled or on‑prem) for full control of egress and KMS.
- Evidence and questionnaire: we agreed HealthGrid will send vendor security questionnaire and procurement contact. We will start populating the questionnaire and provide SOC 2 reports and a BAA draft.

Immediate asks / next steps (owner / ETA):
1) Emily / HealthGrid: share vendor security questionnaire file + procurement contact (procurement@healthgrid.com) — ETA: 48 hours
2) Redwood (Sean): attach SOC 2 summary + BAA summary (attached) and start vendor questionnaire response — ETA: 2 business days
3) Redwood (Monica): schedule a technical design call to review network/PKI/ingress constraints (30–45 min) — proposed Monday 9/13; will confirm availability
4) Procurement: share PO process or redline windows if you require custom BAA language — ETA: 1 week

Attachments: Redwood_BAA_Summary.pdf (brief), I referenced Redwood SOC 2 Type II in the doc.

If that captures it, I can kick off the questionnaire response and loop in Solutions Engineering for the technical session. Would you prefer a short 30-min technical session or a longer 45–60-min review with your security and infra folks?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

Thanks Sean — this is helpful. Quick clarifications from our security/procurement side before we jump into the questionnaire: 

1) SOC 2 evidence: can you confirm whether you can provide a SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) and the auditor name? We typically need the auditor + period for our vendor file.
2) Hosted API question: when you say "Hosted (public) API is not appropriate for PHI," can you confirm if there is any perimeter control (IP allowlist, customer keys) that would let us use the hosted API for low-risk PHI or pseudonymized data? We need to capture the exact boundary in our security matrix.
3) BAA: procurement asked if Redwood can accept our standard BAA template (we will attach it) or if you require your standard BAA. What's your usual path?

I've attached our vendor questionnaire (HealthGrid_Vendor_Q_2026.xlsx) — please fill the sections you can and return. Procurement included: procurement@healthgrid.com for PO/timing.

We can do a 45-minute design + security sync so we can bring the infra folks. Monday 9/13 10:00 AM PT works on our side — does that align?

—Emily

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Emily Wong <emily.wong@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, procurement@healthgrid.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HIPAA access controls, BAA availability and hosting options — action summary

Emily — great questions, answers below inline: 

> 1) SOC 2 evidence: can you confirm whether you can provide a SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) and the auditor name?
Yes — we can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report. Auditor: Sentinel Audit Partners. Period: 2024-07 through 2025-06 (covered controls for the Redwood inference platform). I'll attach the SOC summary and confirm a redacted report delivery timeline (should be within 2 business days).

> 2) Hosted API question: any perimeter control that would allow PHI?
Short answer: No for PHI-in-scope workloads. Details: the hosted multi-tenant API is designed for non-PHI workloads. Controls like IP allowlisting and API keys provide network-level restrictions but do not provide the contractual and isolation guarantees required for PHI under our security policy. For PHI we recommend one of: 
- Dedicated (reserved capacity) with VPC peering and customer-managed ingress (supported via Redwood Dedicated)
- Redwood Private deployment (customer VPC or on-prem) for full egress control and KMS integration
We will include this language in the BAA summary so you can map it to your security matrix.

> 3) BAA: can you accept HealthGrid template or need Redwood template?
We typically start with Redwood's standard BAA and are open to reviewing customer redlines. To speed the process, many customers send their template and we perform a targeted legal review. If HealthGrid prefers, attach your BAA and we'll have Legal review in parallel with questionnaire completion.

I've started filling the attached questionnaire and included a draft response workbook (Redwood_Vendor_Questionnaire_Response_draft.xlsx) — you'll see high-level answers in the vendor controls tab. We'll follow up with the redacted SOC 2 and the BAA draft.

Also confirming: Monday 9/13 10:00 AM PT for the technical + security sync works for us. Monica will schedule and send out calendar invite.

Thanks,
Sean

(Attachment: Redwood_Vendor_Questionnaire_Response_draft.xlsx)
